Where AI Money Went in 2026

AI took about two-thirds of global venture funding in Q3 2026. Where the largest rounds went, which bets are crowded, which are quiet, and how exposed each kind of company is to the frontier labs.

$102B ↑AI venture, Q3 2026 ⚠️
64% ↑of all venture funding ⚠️
27 ↑rounds of $1B+ ⚠️
−33% ↓Q3 vs Q2 (CB Insights) ⚠️
Home›AI Market Map›Foundations · Brief 3 of 6
FR
FrontierAGI Research
November 18, 2026 · 7 min read · ⚠️ = secondary source
Key takeawaysThe moneyCrowded and quiet betsThe wrapper testMethod and sources

⚡ Key takeaways

💡
  1. AI start-ups raised about $102B in Q3 2026, 64% of all global venture funding (Crunchbase, reported).
  2. A record 27 rounds of $1B or more; the largest went to infrastructure and data platforms that sell to the labs.
  3. CB Insights counts $103.3B for Q3, down 33% from Q2: money is concentrating in fewer, larger rounds.
  4. Coding agents are the most crowded bet and the most exposed to the labs.
  5. Robotics, compute and verification are the least exposed; verification has few well-funded independents.

So what: Infrastructure is where the money is safest from the labs, because the labs are its customers.

📊 Crowded and quiet bets

🎯
Thesis 2: Coding agents are crowded; compute, robotics and verification are quiet.medium confidence
🔧 Reproduce this: entrant_map.py
entrant_map.py · reads data/ai-entrants-2026.json
"""entrant_map.py — where new AI companies cluster, and how exposed they are to the labs.

Reads data/ai-entrants-2026.json (a hand-curated, sourced sample, not a census) and
groups companies by layer: how many, how many valuations are reported, and the
average 'lab overlap' (our 0-3 judgement of how directly frontier labs compete).
Standard library only.
"""
import json, os
d = json.load(open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "..", "ai-entrants-2026.json")))
by = {}
for x in d["items"]: by.setdefault(x["layer"], []).append(x)
print(f"{'layer':11} {'companies':>9} {'avg lab overlap':>15}  examples")
for layer, xs in sorted(by.items(), key=lambda kv: -sum(x["overlap"] for x in kv[1]) / len(kv[1])):
    ov = sum(x["overlap"] for x in xs) / len(xs)
    print(f"{layer:11} {len(xs):9d} {ov:15.1f}  {', '.join(x['name'] for x in xs[:3])}")
hi = [x["name"] for x in d["items"] if x["overlap"] >= 3]; lo = [x["name"] for x in d["items"] if x["overlap"] == 0]
print(f"most exposed to the labs (3/3): {len(hi)}; least exposed (0/3): {len(lo)} -> {', '.join(lo)}")
$ python3 entrant_map.py layer companies avg lab overlap examples harness 2 3.0 Cognition, Cursor (Anysphere) models 6 2.7 Thinking Machines Lab, Safe Superintelligence (SSI), Mistral AI frameworks 2 2.0 LangChain, CrewAI builders 2 1.5 n8n, Zapier apps 3 1.3 Harvey, Sierra, River AI data 1 1.0 Databricks runtimes 1 1.0 Temporal compute 4 0.0 Crusoe, CoreWeave, Groq physical 2 0.0 Unitree Robotics, Walden Robotics most exposed to the labs (3/3): 6; least exposed (0/3): 6 -> Crusoe, CoreWeave, Unitree Robotics, Walden Robotics, Groq, Cerebras

Real script output on a 23-company sourced sample (not a census); overlap scores are our judgement.

👉
So what: A start-up's risk is less about its funding than about whether the next lab release does its job.

🧭 The wrapper test

  • Would the next model release make this company unnecessary?
    • High risk: thin prompts and interfaces over a model the lab also sells.
    • Lower risk: value in data, workflow, distribution, hardware or trust the lab does not have.

📄 Method and sources

  • Totals and rounds as reported by Crunchbase and CB Insights (via Lexology) and press; secondary ⚠️.
  • Entrant sample: data/ai-entrants-2026.json, 23 companies, each with a source.
  • Lab-overlap scores are our judgement.
⚠️
Facts are sourced; figures marked ⚠️ come from secondary reports or company statements. Scores, weights and predictions are our judgement and are labelled.
